synopsis: Relapsing polychondritis is described as an immune-mediated disease of recurrent inflammation in cartilage and proteoglycan-rich tissue: elastic cartilage of the ear and nose, hyaline cartilage of peripheral joints, fibrocartilage at axial sites, and tracheobronchial cartilage, leading to deformation and functional loss. In over 80% of patients it presents with auricular chondritis and polyarthritis. Onset is often insidious, with painful crises and spontaneous remissions, which delays diagnosis. Another autoimmune disease is present in 30% of adult patients, most often rheumatoid arthritis. Airway disease thickens the tracheal wall and destroys cartilage rings. Tracheomalacia can collapse the airway. Chronic inflammation produces strictures, subglottic inflammation, tracheal collapse, and secondary pulmonary infection. Airway intervention often requires balloon dilatation, stent placement, tracheotomy, or a combination.
